security_audit.summary: Three temporary-file writes pose overwrite and symlink risks because they use predictable paths in a shared directory. The remaining 33 alerts concern Markdown formatting, public government data, local parsing, or readable multilingual text rather than dangerous behavior. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:22, 34, and 46 write calendar downloads to predictable shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private directory with mktemp -d, quote its paths, and use it for all downloads and reads. Remove it on exit.

content.user_title: Check Taiwan Holidays and Government Workdays
content.value_statement: Taiwan holiday dates and government workdays can change when official calendars are revised. This skill guides official CSV lookups and XLSX cross-checks without API keys.
actual_capabilities: Look up government holidays and workdays using official calendar CSV files.
Identify makeup workdays and deferred holidays from calendar status fields and remarks.
Support long-weekend queries by comparing consecutive dates in the government calendar.
Handle UTF-8 BOM, Big5 encoding, and CRLF line endings in calendar files.
Use the revised 2025 calendar to avoid missing holidays added later that year.
Cross-check CSV results with official XLSX calendar cell styles using a Python standard-library recipe.
limitations: The government calendar does not determine company, school, bank, or stock-market schedules.
Lookups require network access and a host capable of running the documented shell commands.
Official attachment links and calendar revisions require checking the latest government listings.
The XLSX parser uses layout and style constants that must be revalidated for different workbooks.

use_cases.title: Plan Government Staff Leave
use_cases.description: Compare official holidays and adjacent workdays before selecting leave dates.

use_cases.title: Check Travel Dates
use_cases.description: Find government-calendar long weekends before choosing travel dates, while checking service-specific opening schedules separately.

use_cases.title: Validate Workday Rules
use_cases.description: Compare scheduling assumptions with official CSV status fields and cross-check important results against the published workbook.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Date
prompt_templates.prompt: Is [YYYY-MM-DD] a Taiwan government workday or holiday? Use the official calendar and cite the source.

prompt_templates.title: List Monthly Days Off
prompt_templates.prompt: List Taiwan government days off in [year and month]. Include dates, weekdays, remarks, and the official source.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Long Weekends
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Taiwan government long weekends between [start date] and [end date]. Show consecutive days off, nearby workdays, and source revision details.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Check Calendar Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [year] government holidays using the latest official CSV and XLSX. Check encoding, revisions, and parser constants. Report discrepancies and use private temporary files.

output_examples.input: Is January 1, 2026 a Taiwan government holiday?
output_examples.output: January 1, 2026 is Thursday and a government day off. Source: the 2026 DGPA calendar example documented in this skill.

output_examples.input: Which late September 2026 dates form a government-calendar long weekend?
output: The documented 2026 calendar indicates four consecutive days off from September 25 through September 28.
September 25 and September 28 are weekday holidays. September 26 and September 27 are weekend dates.
Verify the latest DGPA announcement before booking. Company and service schedules may differ.

best_practices: Check the latest official revision for the requested year and cite the calendar source.
Confirm file encoding and line endings, then validate XLSX layout constants before using fallback results.
Use private temporary files and verify important scheduling decisions against the official announcement.
anti_patterns: Treating the government calendar as a company, school, bank, or stock-market schedule.
Using the original 2025 CSV without checking the later official revision.
Reusing expired attachment links or spreadsheet style constants without validating the current file.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key or login?
faq.answer: No. It uses public government calendar downloads without API keys or authentication.

faq.question: Which calendar does it use?
faq.answer: It uses DGPA government administrative office calendars and Taiwan open-data dataset 14718.

faq.question: Which years are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents ROC years 106 through 116, equivalent to 2017 through 2027. Confirm current availability on the dataset page.

faq.question: Does it cover school or stock-market holidays?
faq.answer: No. Schools, banks, companies, and stock markets can follow different calendars that require separate sources.

faq.question: How does it identify makeup workdays?
faq.answer: It checks workday status and the makeup-workday remark. The skill states that the adjustment system ended in late 2025; verify current announcements.

faq.question: What happens if a download fails or looks corrupted?
faq.answer: Find the latest attachment on the official listing, check encoding, and use the XLSX fallback after validating its layout and styles.
